actions.action: Free replacement card on request and payment alerts
Instant dispute credit up to $100 per customer, 8 weeks

decisions.message: Update on the card charges from Nov 16-17: our card processor confirmed a fault that charged some payments twice, and a small number of cards had fraud test charges of $0.50 to $2 after card numbers were stolen elsewhere, for example on a fake shopping site. Cobalt's own systems were not breached. About 9,000 customers were affected. Starting today, for 8 weeks: if you dispute a card charge, we credit up to $100 right away while we investigate. In the app you can turn on an alert for every card payment and order a free new card.
why: The week-4 facts are far smaller than the 'Cobalt got hacked' rumor, but many customers only heard the rumor.
Instant dispute credit and payment alerts give every customer a concrete way to protect themselves before the migration.
We repeat only what the processor confirmed and promise nothing about refunds we cannot yet confirm.

decisions.target: paycheck customers who work for the federal government or its contractors

actions.action: Zero-interest advance up to $500, up to 20,000 customers

decisions.message: If your pay is delayed by the government shutdown because you work for the federal government or a federal contractor, you can ask Cobalt for a zero-interest advance of up to $500. No fees and no interest. The offer covers up to 20,000 customers, in the order requests arrive. Request it in the app. We cannot say how long the shutdown will last; we will tell you as soon as we know more.
why: The week-7 shutdown leaves federal and contractor paycheck customers with no pay date before Christmas bills.
A zero-interest advance up to $500 for up to 20,000 customers covers the roughly 10-15k we estimate are affected, before the Dec 30 paycheck is missed.
It costs $0.4M, $1.35M in total with decision 1, and helps the people hit hardest without buying loyalty with rate offers.
